searchText: Hi, I've got a pretty noobish question..... Why **exactly** can't ethereum sync without an SSD? Example: I've got plain-vanilla default `geth` running on a machine with a 3- HDD raid 0 setup, and while I failed to configure geth (I literally invoked it as `geth` and saw "oh, it's working" and walked away a few days ago) properly when I started it to ensure that I could check its status, my logs be like: ``` INFO [05-04|08:57:36.653] Imported new state entries count=700 elapsed=3.485ms processed=225903592 pending=16554 retry=0 duplicate=83131 unexpected=224779 INFO [05-04|08:57:37.568] Imported new block headers count=1 elapsed=3.726ms number=9998217 hash=3f867f…28fe24 age=1m5s INFO [05-04|08:57:38.530] Imported new state entries count=1084 elapsed=5.970ms processed=225904676 pending=15678 retry=0 duplicate=83131 unexpected=224779 INFO [05-04|08:57:40.222] Imported new state entries count=1014 elapsed=4.481ms processed=225905690 pending=16477 retry=69 duplicate=83131 unexpected=224779 ``` So I assume it's still syncing. Guess I'm hoping for a precise answer instead of the kinds of answers I might get if I asked on Twitter. Thank you! (Please feel free to point me at relevant docs or what have you, I want to fully understand why this is the case.) <jadler> You can get precise answers on Twitter, e.g. https://twitter.com/jadler0/status/1162007432111022081 <jadler> That being said, your question is outside the scope of this channel. <@!358350138428882947> it's indeed out of scope of this channel, but it's a question we get so often over at go-ethereum that we have a standard answer. I'll try and stay in-scope in the future 🙂 <GuthL> Does this answer still hold in the context of Beam Sync of Stateless Eth assuming not full sync in the background? (@tkstanczak) <GuthL> Sorry if this is also out of scope <jadler> Beam Sync is a sync protocol, like fast sync, i.e. it's a way to populate the initial state trie. Once the sync part is over, going forward the node will be fully validating blocks, which as described above requires an SSD. TL;DR yes. Now, full statelessness is another matter, since presumably witnesses are small enough to be kept in RAM (they're on the order of a few megabytes per Ethereum block last I checked, with work on reducing that size). excerpts.content:
Hi, I've got a pretty noobish question.....  Why **exactly** can't ethereum sync without an SSD?

Example: I've got plain-vanilla default `geth` running on a machine with a 3- HDD raid 0 setup, and while I failed to configure geth (I literally invoked it as `geth` and saw "oh, it's working" and walked away a few days ago) properly when I started it to ensure that I could check its status, my logs be like:

```
INFO [05-04|08:57:36.653] Imported new state entries               count=700  elapsed=3.485ms   processed=225903592 pending=16554  retry=0   duplicate=83131 unexpected=224779
INFO [05-04|08:57:37.568] Imported new block headers               count=1    elapsed=3.726ms   number=9998217 hash=3f867f…28fe24 age=1m5s
INFO [05-04|08:57:38.530] Imported new state entries               count=1084 elapsed=5.970ms   processed=225904676 pending=15678  retry=0   duplicate=83131 unexpected=224779
INFO [05-04|08:57:40.222] Imported new state entries               count=1014 elapsed=4.481ms   processed=225905690 pending=16477  retry=69  duplicate=83131 unexpected=224779
```

So I assume it's still syncing.  Guess I'm hoping for a precise answer instead of the kinds of answers I might get if I asked on Twitter.  

Thank you!

excerpts.content:
<jadler> Beam Sync is a sync protocol, like fast sync, i.e. it's a way to populate the initial state trie. Once the sync part is over, going forward the node will be fully validating blocks, which as described above requires an SSD.
TL;DR yes.
Now, full statelessness is another matter, since presumably witnesses are small enough to be kept in RAM (they're on the order of a few megabytes per Ethereum block last I checked, with work on reducing that size). (re @GuthL: Does this answer still hold in the context of Beam Sync of Stateless Eth assuming not full sync in the background? (@tkstanczak))
